# Appeal of Denial – Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-24, Reference Number POC-C65CA65DA3-33163**
**Member: Taylor Foster | Member ID: W492196775 | Plan: Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Wyoming**
**Governing Policy: Aetna CPB 0736 – Hip Preservation Surgery (last review 07/31/2026), https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0736.html**

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am writing to request a formal reconsideration of the denial of my prior authorization request for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), as described in the notice above. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary for my condition, and I am asking the plan to review this decision.

## Why I am appealing

The stated reason for denial is that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I want to address this directly, and I also want to raise a concern about which policy criteria were used to evaluate my request.

**The policy language I have been given does not appear to match my situation.** The excerpts from Aetna CPB 0736 that were provided to support this denial address pelvic osteotomy (including peri-acetabular osteotomy) for acetabular dysplasia, iliopsoas tenotomy following total hip arthroplasty, and repair of complete gluteus medius tears. For example, the policy states:

> "Aetna considers pelvic osteotomy (e.g., peri-acetabular osteotomy (PAO)) medically necessary for a diagnosis of acetabular dysplasia (not borderline dysplasia) for persons who fulfill all of the following criteria:"

and

> "Arthroscopic surgery in concert with an osteotomy would be assessed using the medical necessity criteria noted above for arthroscopic surgery of the hip."

My diagnosis, as documented in my MRI arthrogram of 2026-07-11, is an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement (alpha angle 68 degrees), with joint space preserved and Tonnis grade 0. This is not acetabular dysplasia, I am not having a pelvic osteotomy, and I am not undergoing iliopsoas tenotomy after a hip replacement or gluteus medius repair. I am not able to find, in the material provided to me, the specific conservative-care criteria that the plan applied to arrive at this denial for a labral tear/FAI arthroscopy. I am asking the plan to identify and provide the specific policy section that applies to arthroscopic treatment of a labral tear with FAI, and to explain how that section, rather than the pelvic-osteotomy or arthroplasty-related sections quoted to me, supports this denial.

**Separately, my records show significant conservative treatment was completed before surgery was requested.** Regardless of which specific criteria apply, the record shows:

- **Symptom duration:** 24 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Physical therapy:** 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, 18 visits completed between 2026-04-27 and 2026-08-03, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-14, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Functional limitation:** Sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and inability to run or squat.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

I have also been told that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I do not smoke.

I recognize that Aetna's own policy states that "these supplemental medical necessity criteria are based upon evidence-based guidelines and clinical studies in the peer-reviewed published medical literature," and I am asking that the specific criteria applicable to my diagnosis and procedure be applied to the conservative-care history above.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Aetna to reverse this denial, or, at minimum, to identify the specific policy section applicable to arthroscopic treatment of a labral tear with FAI and to re-review my case against that section in light of the conservative treatment already documented in my records.

I understand that this appeal does not guarantee that the decision will be changed, but I believe my records support reconsideration.

## Deadline and where I am sending this

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-20** (180 days from the date of denial), though I am confirming the exact appeal address on my denial letter as instructed. I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com, under complaints, grievances and appeals), and/or by fax to 859-425-3379, and/or by mail to the address printed on my denial letter. I can also be reached by phone at 1-800-872-3862 if additional information is needed.

Thank you for reviewing my appeal.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Foster**
Member ID: W492196775
[Address]

Date: [Date of submission]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

for members with moderate or worse arthritis (Tonnis 2 or 3), the procedure would be considered not medically necessary;
Aetna considers pelvic osteotomy in skeletally immature children medically necessary for a diagnosis of acetabular dysplasia.
Arthroscopic surgery in concert with an osteotomy would be assessed using the medical necessity criteria noted above for arthroscopic surgery of the hip.
Medically Necessary Procedures Medically necessary procedures, when above criteria are met, include:

Endoscopic tenotomy (or lengthening) for iliopsoas tendinopathy following total hip arthroplasty with the failure of at least 6 weeks of formal in-person physical therapy in the past year, and at least 1 therapeutic injection (steroid with or without local anesthetic) with significant but temporary benefit in the past 6 months.
Repair of complete gluteus medius tears is considered medically necessary.

The supplemental medical necessity criteria in this CPB further define those indications for services that are proven safe and effective where those indications are not fully established in applicable NCDs and LCDs.
These supplemental medical necessity criteria are based upon evidence-based guidelines and clinical studies in the peer-reviewed published medical literature.

The background section of this CPB includes an explanation of the rationale that supports adoption of the medical necessity criteria and a summary of evidence that was considered during the development of the CPB;

While there is a possible risk of reduced or delayed care with any coverage criteria, Aetna believes that the benefits of these criteria – ensuring patients receive services that are appropriate, safe, and effective – substantially outweigh any clinical harms.
